propositions.text: Claimant alleges well-founded fear of persecution in Dominican Republic for Convention reasons and risk to life or torture.
propositions.quote: XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX Sanchez is a citizen of the Dominican Republic who claims Convention refugee status and refugee protection in Canada based on his allege well-founded fear of persecution in the Dominican Republic for Convention reasons and the alleged risk there to his life, risk of cruel and unusual punishment or treatment, or danger of torture.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges a well-founded fear of persecution and risk of harm in the Dominican Republic, seeking refugee protection.

propositions.text: Minister alleges claimant should be excluded from refugee protection for committing serious non-political crime outside country of refuge before admission.
propositions.quote: The Minister has filed a Notice of Intervention alleging that the claimant should be excluded from refugee protection considering that he has committed a serious non-political crime outside the country of refuge prior to his admission to that country as a refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister alleges the claimant should be excluded from refugee protection due to serious non-political crimes committed before admission.

propositions.text: Claimant is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1(f) of the refugee Convention and is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Based on the evidence and submissions, the claimant is a person referred to in section (f) of Article 1 of the refugee Convention and is thereby not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. The claimant is excluded from the refugee determination process.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1(f) and is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Claimant was convicted in USA in 1998 of assault with a weapon and received three years probation after pleading guilty.
propositions.quote: In 1998, the claimant was convicted in the United States of America (USA) of assault with a weapon and received three years probation. He pleaded guilty to the charge of assault with intent to cause physical harm.

propositions.text: In 2004, claimant was convicted in USA of possession with intent to traffic and served five years probation, pleading guilty.
propositions.quote: In the year 2004, again in the USA, he was convicted of possession with intent to traffic and served five years probation. He appears to have negotiated the guilty pleas on both of these offences.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant was convicted in the USA in 1998 and 2004 for assault and drug trafficking, receiving probation after guilty pleas.

propositions.text: Claimant explains 1998 assault involved a woman who propositioned him, then broke window and injured herself; he struck her with plastic tube.
propositions.quote: The claimant explained, with respect to the first conviction from 1998, that he was followed to his room by a woman who propositioned to have sexual intercourse with him for money. When he said no, she left but then returned, kicked and broke his window and thereby injured herself. He added that he struck her with a plastic tube and threw it at her.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant explains the 1998 assault involved a woman who broke a window and he struck her with a plastic tube.

propositions.text: Claimant's evidence about 1998 assault was inconsistent and inadequately resolved, with contradictions about timing and details.
propositions.quote: On a careful assessment of the evidence in this area of the claim, I find that the claimant's evidence wavered materially and the story that he put forward was fraught with inconsistencies and discrepancies which remained inadequately resolved.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant's evidence about the 1998 assault inconsistent and inadequately resolved.

propositions.text: Court rejects claimant's explanation and finds incident did not occur as alleged or was not precipitated by victim's conduct on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: I reject this explanation and find that it has not been established on a balance of probabilities that the incident occurred in the way alleged or was precipitated by the conduct of the female victim.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the claimant's explanation and finds the incident did not occur as alleged or was precipitated by the victim.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges he has served his sentence for the 1998 crime.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that he has served his sentence in connection with the 1998 crime.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he served his sentence for the 1998 crime.

propositions.text: Claimant explains 2004 conviction involved selling cocaine during brief unemployment to support ill family members.
propositions.quote: In 2004, the claimant was convicted of possession with intent to sell. His counsel negotiated a guilty plea in exchange for five years probation. He stated that in the year 2003, he sold, one day apart, six grams of cocaine and made a profit of $120. He claims that he never sold cocaine either before or after this. He alleges that he only sold cocaine because he had been unemployed for a two-week period when he was laid off from full-time employment at an XXXXXXXXX which closed down subsequently. The claimant states that he was re-employed at another XXXXXXXXX right away, but during those two weeks of unemployment, he was arrested. He explained that he had told a friend about his mother's illness whereupon the friend offered that he could sell drugs for money. The claimant went on to allege that his mother had suffered a stroke and was very ill. He stated that she needed medication and that he was sending money to his father. He stated that his mother died and that his father was elderly, had back problems and was not working. He added that his sister suffered from epilepsy and was also not working. By the date of the hearing, there was no independent corroboration regarding either his own employment situation or his family's heath status at material times. His explanation for these critical evidentiary shortcomings was that he did not think it necessary to obtain and supply the information.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant explains the 2004 conviction involved selling cocaine during brief unemployment to support ill family members, but lacks corroboration.

propositions.text: Court rejects claimant's explanation for lack of corroboration as inadequate in refugee claim context.
propositions.quote: I reject this explanation and find it significantly inadequate in the highly important circumstances of a refugee claim, and particularly one that engages the issues that have been set out in his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the claimant's explanation for lack of corroboration as inadequate in this refugee claim.

propositions.text: Claimant says he can obtain receipts and records to corroborate allegations and requests one week to submit them without reconvening hearing.
propositions.quote: The claimant said that he could obtain and proffer receipts and other records to corroborate the allegations he has made at his hearing. His counsel applied for leave to obtain, gather and submit corroborating documentation to help support these allegations and explanations, seeking one week to do so and submitting that it would not be necessary to reconvene the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant offers to obtain corroborating documents and requests one week to submit them without reconvening the hearing.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant did not adequately explain failure to submit corroboration timely; counsel did not address this.
propositions.quote: The Panel ruled that it was not established on balance that the claimant had adequately explained the reasons for his failure to do what was now being requested, in a timely manner and well in advance of his hearing. He had been represented at material times by counsel who is a barrister and solicitor having experience presenting immigration and refugee claims. The claimant's assertion that he did not think it necessary to obtain and submit such corroboration is not satisfactory or credible and was not addressed in any way by his counsel in the course of the application.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant failed to adequately explain late request for corroboration and counsel did not address it.

propositions.text: Extensive corroboration was filed for refugee allegations, showing claimant knew importance of timely documentation; late disclosure rejected.
propositions.quote: Extensive corroboration, including numerous affidavits, was filed in connection with the refugee allegations themselves making it clear that the claimant's mind had specifically been turned to the importance of filing supporting documentation in advance. I therefore reject the late disclosure.

propositions.text: There were substantial discrepancies between oral testimony and PIF about claimant's employment period with alleged employer.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, there were substantial discrepancies between the oral testimony and work history section of the Personal Information Form (PIF)1 relating to the claimant's place and period of employment with the employer by whom he alleged to have been laid off.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects late disclosure and finds discrepancies between oral testimony and PIF about employment period.

propositions.text: Claimant testified he was laid off in 2003 but PIF states employment from 2001 to 2005; claimant says he cannot recall exact times.
propositions.quote: In oral testimony, the claimant stated that he was laid off by the XXXXXXXXX in 2003. In the PIF, on the other hand, it states that he worked at that XXXXXXXXX between XXXXX 2001 and XXXXX 2005. His explanation for this discrepancy in an important area of his claim was that he could not recall the exact times.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified to being laid off in 2003 but PIF shows employment 2001-2005; he says he cannot recall exact times.

propositions.text: Court rejects claimant's explanation and finds allegations about employment period unreliable without impairment of recall alleged or corroborated.
propositions.quote: Again, I reject this explanation and find that it has not been established on sufficient, reliable evidence that the claimant's allegations in this important area of his claim are reliable. It has not been alleged, much less corroborated and established, that the claimant's ability to recall these or any other timeframes or events either in the PIF or hearing has been impaired or compromised for any reason.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the claimant's explanation and finds employment period allegations unreliable without corroboration or recall impairment.

propositions.text: Despite sentences served, claimant is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1(f)(b) after exhaustive analysis.
propositions.quote: Even though the sentences appear to have been served, based on an exhaustive consideration and analysis of all factors, I find that the claimant is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1(f)(b).

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant excluded from refugee protection under Article 1(f)(b) despite sentences served.

propositions.text: No sufficient mitigating factors exist to determine claimant's criminal conduct was not serious non-political crimes under all circumstances.
propositions.quote: Based on a consideration and analysis of all the factors engaged by the issue of exclusion in this case, I find that it has not been established that there were sufficient mitigating factors on which to determine that the claimant's criminal conduct in the USA had not been tantamount to serious non-political crimes in all the circumstances before the Division.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no sufficient mitigating factors to avoid exclusion for serious non-political crimes.

propositions.text: Court relies on Minister's submissions on serious crime definition and finds claimant's crimes serious under Canadian law; serving sentence does not absolve exclusion.
propositions.quote: In coming to this conclusion, I have relied heavily on the submissions and reply of counsel for the Minister. In particular, I have been assisted by and agree with her treatment of what constitutes a serious crime in Canada. I find that the crimes committed by the claimant are serious crimes under Canadian law, and the question of whether or not he served one or more of his sentences does not absolve him from the point of view of assessment of exclusion from the refugee determination process and the state of the current Canadian jurisprudence on Article 1(f)(b).

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with Minister that claimant's crimes are serious under Canadian law and serving sentence does not prevent exclusion.

propositions.text: Division is not required to examine inclusionary elements after finding claimant excluded under Article 1(f)(b).
propositions.quote: The Division is not required to proceed onto an examination and analysis of the inclusionary elements of the claimant's refugee claim having found the claimant excluded under Article 1(f)(b).

paragraphs.summary: The Division need not examine inclusionary elements after finding exclusion under Article 1(f)(b).

propositions.text: Claimant is excluded under Article 1(f)(b) for committing serious non-political crimes outside country of refuge before admission.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, based on the submissions of both counsels and the evidence properly before me, I conclude that the claimant is excluded under Article 1(f)(b) of the Convention as he has committed serious non-political crimes outside the country of refuge prior to his admission to that country as a refugee.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the claimant is excluded under Article 1(f)(b) for serious non-political crimes committed before admission.
